title: RhymeQ Emerges from Stealth with $2.2 Million Pre-Seed Round to Launch Python Abstraction Layer for Quantum Computing - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Karlsruhe and Zurich-based RhymeQ emerged from stealth with a $2.2M pre-seed led by Ground State Ventures to offer Rhyme, a Python abstraction layer for quantum programming that compiles to NVIDIA CUDA-Q. It was unveiled at NVIDIA GTC Berlin.

insights.claim: RhymeQ raised $2.2 million USD in pre-seed financing led by Ground State Ventures, with participation from Vanagon Ventures, Plug and Play and Freiraum Ventures.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Tiny round; software abstraction startups are early and capital-light.
insights.locator: Karlsruhe and Zürich-based quantum software startup

insights.claim: The capital will expand the engineering team, accelerate enterprise platform integration and grow the developer waitlist community.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Waitlist stage indicates the product is not yet broadly available.

insights.claim: RhymeQ's Rhyme platform is an abstraction layer letting developers with standard Python proficiency program and debug quantum software without low-level circuit compilation or gate-level hardware expertise.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Lowering the skills barrier widens the quantum developer pool, a bottleneck for adoption.

insights.claim: Rhyme compiles directly to the NVIDIA CUDA-Q framework, enabling execution across GPU-accelerated simulators and multiple physical quantum processor architectures without hardware lock-in.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: More startups building on CUDA-Q reinforces NVIDIA's role as quantum software hub.
